title: Bozcaada Island Guide: Vineyards, Windmills & Quiet Aegean Beaches

quickAnswer: Reached by a 35-minute GESTAŞ ferry from Geyikli Pier, Bozcaada pairs centuries-old Aegean vineyards with clear southern coves like Ayazma and Akvaryum Koyu, sunset views at Polente Lighthouse, and stone boutique hotels in its Greek Quarter. Book vehicle ferries and stone inns two to three months ahead for summer stays.

body.text: How does the Geyikli ferry to Bozcaada work?

Car and passenger ferries operated by GESTAŞ depart from Geyikli Yükyeri Pier on the Çanakkale mainland and reach Bozcaada Harbor in about 35 minutes, running five or more daily sailings during winter and expanded high-frequency departures throughout peak summer weekends and holidays.

Because ferry schedules shift between winter and summer seasons, always verify exact sailing times on the [GESTAŞ ferry timetable](https://gdu.com.tr/sefer-tarifeleri) and reserve vehicle spots through [GESTAŞ online ticketing](https://gdu.com.tr/online-bilet). Crossing times average [35 minutes](https://www.feribotseferleri.com.tr/seferler/geyikli-bozcaada), dropping you directly beneath Bozcaada Castle. If you travel on foot during July or August, leaving your rental car in the guarded lot at Geyikli Pier often saves hours of boarding queues—especially on Sunday afternoons when mainland return lines peak.

Bozcaada's volcanic soils, bright sunshine, and steady northern winds sustain six documented island wineries, with Corvus, Çamlıbağ, Talay, and Amadeus offering the most rewarding structured tastings of indigenous Kuntra, Karalahna, and Vasilaki grapes alongside international varietals in both estates and town cellars.

Viticulture on ancient Tenedos stretches back to antiquity, highlighted on [Go Türkiye's Bozcaada Vineyard Route](https://goturkiye.com/vineyards/bozcaada-vineyard-route). Each producer offers a distinct experience:

items: Çamlıbağ Winery: Founded in 1925 by the Yunatçı family, [Çamlıbağ](https://troiawineroute.com/en/guardians-of-heritage/camlibag-winery/) operates 30 hectares of vineyards and welcomes visitors at both its island estate and its town tasting shop for native Vasilaki, Kuntra, and Karalahna pours.

Corvus Vineyards: Established in 2002 by architect Reşit Soley across 25 hectares at Tuzburnu Bay, [Corvus](https://www.winewithseth.com/winewiki/corvus-bozcaada-tenedos-island-aegean/) produces over 20 wines and runs a central tasting room in Bozcaada town.

Amadeus Winery: Founded in 2010 by the Austrian Gareis family, [Amadeus](https://www.vitikultur.com/en/wineries/amadeus-bozcaada/) grows rare Sicilian Grillo alongside Syrah and Chardonnay; visits and tastings operate by appointment.
Talay and Ataol: Both long-standing family estates offer accessible town-center tastings and retail bottles, ideal for pairing with late-afternoon mezze.

body.text: Where are the clearest beaches (Ayazma, Akvaryum)?

The clearest swimming water sits along Bozcaada's sheltered southern coast, led by sandy Ayazma Beach for full amenities and rocky Akvaryum Koyu (Mermer Burnu) for snorkeling, while western Polente Lighthouse and its 17 wind turbines deliver the island's signature sunset.

Because the northern Poyraz wind blows reliably across the North Aegean, locals choose coves by daily wind direction. According to the [Bozcaada District Governorship beach guide](https://bozcaada.gov.tr/plajlar), seasonal minibuses connect the town center directly to Ayazma, Sulubahçe, Habbele, and Mermer Burnu (Akvaryum Koyu).

body.text: Before dusk, drive or take a local taxi to Polente Lighthouse on the western cape, where Bozcaada's wind turbines frame open views toward Gökçeada and the Aegean horizon.
When should you book stone boutique hotels?

Book Bozcaada's restored Greek Quarter stone inns and vineyard guesthouses three to four months ahead for July, August, and Turkish public holidays, or four to six weeks ahead for quieter shoulder-season stays in May, June, September, and October when weather remains mild.

Bozcaada has no large resort chains; accommodation consists of intimate 6-to-15-room stone houses in Alaybey (the historic Greek Quarter) and small vineyard properties (bağ evi) inland. Use this planning checklist before locking in your dates:

items: Target shoulder months: Late May–June and September–early October combine warm sea temperatures with open wineries and calmer streets.
Check harvest festival dates: Early September grape-harvest weekends fill every room months in advance.
Match location to transport: Choose Alaybey if arriving without a car; pick a vineyard hotel only if you have a vehicle or pre-arranged transfers.
Confirm breakfast and parking: Historic stone streets are largely pedestrianized, so verify where luggage drop-off and parking sit.

faq.q: How long is the Geyikli to Bozcaada ferry crossing?
faq.a: The GESTAŞ car and passenger ferry from Geyikli Yükyeri Pier to Bozcaada Harbor takes approximately 35 minutes, though you should arrive early during summer weekends to clear boarding queues.

faq.q: Do I need to book Bozcaada ferry tickets online in advance?
faq.a: Yes, especially if you are bringing a car between June and September. GESTAŞ offers online reservations for vehicles, while foot passengers can buy tickets at the pier or online.

faq.q: Which Bozcaada wineries are best for tastings?
faq.a: Leading stops include Corvus for modern estate tastings, Çamlıbağ for historic island vintages since 1925, Talay for accessible town-center tastings, and Amadeus for small-batch whites by appointment.

faq.q: Which Bozcaada beach has the clearest water for snorkeling?
faq.a: Akvaryum Koyu (Mermer Burnu) is widely known for its transparent water and fish life, though it has no beach club facilities. Bring water, shade, and snorkel gear.

faq.q: Can I explore Bozcaada without a car?
faq.a: Yes. Municipal minibuses run regularly from the harbor square to Ayazma, Sulubahçe, Habbele, and Akvaryum Koyu during the warm season, and the historic town center is completely walkable.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Bozcaada for fewer crowds?
faq.a: Late May to mid-June and mid-September to early October offer warm swimming water, active winery tastings, harvest atmosphere, and far calmer ferry lines than July and August.
